The script does no recoding (as.numeric only), and live per-item counts reproduce the raw file exactly: baseline 1551/2159/2365 ones of n=2365, month-12 571/1052/1756 ones of n=2209 (156 '#NULL!' cells dropped). RIGHTS: study-specific three-item block with no named rights holder; nothing reserving a right located, deposit CC0. DATA CAVEAT (response table, not text): the baseline wave looks defective -- item 3 is constant (2365/2365 = 1), baseline items 1-2 intercorrelate only +0.086 against +0.57 at month 12, and each baseline item correlates -0.014 to +0.036 with its own month-12 response. Reported, not fixed. RETRY TEST: n/a (written).
public_note: Wording and Yes/No labels are the study codebook's English; the trial was administered in Chinese and no Chinese wording is deposited. Note that resp=1 means 'Yes' for item 1 but 'No' for items 2 and 3, so 1 is the stigmatising answer throughout. The baseline wave (wave 1) looks unreliable: every one of 2,365 respondents answered 1 to item 3, and baseline answers are essentially uncorrelated with each other (r=0.09 for items 1-2, against 0.57 at 12 months) and with the same person's 12-month answers (r between -0.01 and 0.04).

Rights: deposit CC0 1.0; the list is Goldberg's own adjective inventory published in full by him in the deposit; grep of the PDF text for copyright/permission/reserved returns nothing; instrument_rights_register.csv has no row for this list (the BSRI row matched on 'adjective' but is keyed ^bsri and is a different instrument); no fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause located (silence, not a positive grant); no register row written.
